title: microbench-suite-for-kernel-routing-and-prefill-scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We need a compact, repeatable microbenchmarking harness that isolates latency/throughput differences caused by kernel selection, attention path optimizations, and prefill vs decode scheduling strategies. Current end-to-end workloads mix network, batching, and caching effects which make small kernel-level regressions hard to detect in CI.

Goals / Success criteria:
- Provide a lightweight suite of 6–8 targeted workloads (synthetic and production-derived) that exercise: kernel dispatch for varying head counts & block sizes, flash attention vs fused-attention paths, KV cache priming patterns, prefill-only, decode-only, and mixed prefill+decode flows.
- Produce reproducible "golden" baseline artifacts (JSON metrics + raw token trace samples) per model family and target hardware (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, 8xV100 cluster baseline).
- Add CI perf gates that compare PR-run metrics to goldens using a stable outlier-resistant metric (median latency and 95th-percentile decode throughput over N runs).
- Integrate artifacts into S3 (benchmarks/goldens/runtime-1.20/) and expose time-series to Grafana for trend monitoring.

Acceptance criteria:
- New harness supports parameterized kernel selector flags and attention-mode toggles via CLI and SDK harness API.
- Golden artifacts generated for model-7B, model-13B (fp16/q4 variants) on target hardware images.
- CI perf gates run on nightly and PR lanes; a PR fails if median latency regresses >6% and p95 decode throughput decreases >7% compared to nearest golden (statistically significant at p<0.05 with bootstrap).
- Documentation (Confluence) and README with reproducibility steps, artifact naming, and TTL/retention policy.

Planned approach:
1) Define microbench workload templates (prefill-only short, prefill-long then decode short, streaming decode with KV hits/misses, attention stress test with long sequence lengths). Store templates in benchmarks/workloads/.
2) Implement harness shim (bench-runner) that can toggle runtime flags: --kernel-selector=<auto|latency|throughput>, --attention-mode=<fused|flash|naive>, --priming-pattern=<random|prefix|kv-primed>. Ensure warm-up policy and clock sync are deterministic.
3) Run experiments on dedicated infra lab and capture raw traces plus metrics: tokens/sec, median latency (ms), p95 latency, GPU utilization, SM occupancy, memory footprint.
4) Create golden artifact schema: flat JSON fields (model, hw, commit, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, sample_traces[] (base64), note). Upload to S3 path with commit-tagged and canonical symlink.
5) CI integration: add bench compare step to our GH actions matrix. Use 3 repeated runs per job, compute bootstrap CI. Fail PRs that exceed thresholds. Nightly job refreshes rolling baselines subject to manual review.

Trade-offs and decisions to make:
- Sample count vs CI cost: default 3 runs per job balances sensitivity and time; can increase for nightly.
- Metric selection: median is robust to outliers; p95 still required for tail behavior. We will avoid mean for latency.
- Golden drift policy: roll forward goldens via a gated process (bench-review:manual) not automatic.

Artifacts / Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Microbench+Harnes+s+Design (stub)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/412
- Grafana dashboard (perf-lab): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/benchmarking/runtime-kernel-routing
- S3 staging: s3://redwood-benchmarks/staging/runtime-1.20/

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- ENG: implement bench-runner toggle flags (owner: Marco) — block: need infra image with latest kernels (ENG-9851)
- Ops: allocate 3 lab runs for the first pass (request submitted ticket infra-342)
- QA: draft CI perf gate logic and expected false-positive rate handling

Notes on measurement rigor:
- Use wall-clock aligned to host monotonic clock; hide GC/collection metadata by filtering background processes.
- For KV cache priming tests, ensure deterministic prefix sequences (seeded RNG).
- Compare like-for-like by pinning sequence lengths and batch size; capture per-token latencies during decode to spot per-step regressions.

Longer-term
- Roll integration into nightly regression dashboard with alerting on sustained drift >3% over 7 days.
